stem: Why do healthcare facilities use water-management programs for building water systems?

options.A: To identify and control conditions that permit Legionella and other waterborne pathogens to grow or spread, especially in complex systems serving vulnerable patients.
options.B: To eliminate the need for routine infection-prevention practices whenever tap water meets municipal drinking-water standards.
options.C: To replace all facility plumbing with sterile disposable tubing because building water systems cannot be managed safely.
options.D: To focus only on water taste and odor because healthcare-associated waterborne infections are not a recognized concern.

rationale: CDC recommends comprehensive water-management programs for healthcare facilities to reduce Legionella growth and transmission and to help control other waterborne pathogens. Healthcare facilities often have complex water systems and serve patients at increased risk for severe Legionnaires' disease. WMPs identify hazardous conditions, establish and monitor control measures, define corrective actions, and require ongoing verification/validation. A is correct.
educational_objective: Explain the purpose of healthcare water-management programs: identify and control building-water conditions that permit Legionella and other pathogens to grow or spread, particularly in facilities serving vulnerable populations.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
source_locator: Key Points and Recommendations for Healthcare Facilities: comprehensive WMPs reduce Legionella growth/transmission and can control other waterborne pathogens. About WMPs/Risk in Healthcare Settings: healthcare facilities serve high-risk populations and may have large complex water systems; WMPs identify hazardous conditions and outline control steps.
source_claim_supported: Healthcare water-management programs are used to identify and control conditions that allow Legionella and other waterborne pathogens to grow or spread in building water systems, particularly in facilities serving vulnerable patients.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)

source_original.rationale: CDC recommends comprehensive water-management programs in healthcare facilities to reduce Legionella growth and transmission and help control other waterborne pathogens. source_original.source_detail: Healthcare water-management programs: reduce risk for Legionella growth/transmission and help control other water-related healthcare-associated infections.

correction_summary: Retained key A, added the complex-water-system/vulnerable-patient context from current CDC WMP guidance, and reduced difficulty from hard to medium because the final item tests the direct purpose of the program.

audit_findings.source_authority: CDC Legionella/water-management guidance; NCSBN 2026 Test Plan
audit_findings.exact_locator: Water Management in Healthcare Facilities key points/recommendations plus WMP overview/risk sections
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item accurately explains program purpose without overclaiming sterility or suggesting municipal water standards replace facility-level risk control.

distractor_audit.B: Incorrect because municipal standards do not eliminate the need for facility water-management and infection-prevention practices.
distractor_audit.C: Incorrect because WMPs manage building systems rather than requiring sterile disposable plumbing replacement.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrect because healthcare-associated waterborne pathogens are a recognized patient-safety concern.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A states the actual WMP purpose.
audit_findings.cueing: All alternatives describe possible facility water-program goals.
audit_findings.blueprint: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — environmental hazard management.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Re-read CDC healthcare WMP, general WMP and validation pages, all choices, rationale and NCSBN mapping. A remained uniquely correct.
